reason: The whale needs a motor to turn its attractions, so mounting the motor is a practical first step.
expectation: The motor will be installed on the whale, ready to connect to the drives.

effect: The motor is installed; it now needs connections to the attractions.
reaction: That was a straightforward first step.
reason: The flexible crank coupler looks suited to connecting the motor to the dragon's crank socket.
expectation: The coupler will connect the motor to the dragon's crank.

effect: The dragon is now connected to the motor; the star theatre still needs its drive.
reason: The reducing belt-drive set looks like the remaining connection for running the theatre at a different speed.
expectation: The belt drive will connect the motor to the star theatre at a reduced speed.

effect: The belt drive now turns the star wheel more slowly than the dragon, using different pulley sizes.
reaction: The pulley explanation makes the different speeds easy to understand.
reason: The moving belt and pulleys should be covered before testing the powered attractions.
expectation: The cover will guard the drive while leaving it visible.

effect: The drive is guarded, leaving the accessory switch key as the apparent next step for testing it.
reaction: The cover was a straightforward safety step.
reason: The switch key is the remaining item and should let the guarded drive run.
expectation: The motor will run the dragon and star wheel at their different speeds.

effect: The test confirmed that one switch runs both attractions at different speeds, and revealed that the clutch slips if the dragon is held still.
reaction: Seeing the two mechanisms work together was satisfying; the clutch was an unexpected detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the reducing belt drive was most worthwhile: the different pulley sizes explained clearly why the stars move more slowly than the dragon.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the motor and cover was straightforward but offered less to figure out than the drive connections.

surprise.text: The clutch slipping when the dragon is held still surprised me; I had not expected that detail from the motor assembly.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. The parts had clear roles, although the switch key was mainly an obvious final test.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the linked attractions and the mention of a lifting test make me curious how the complete whale will behave.
